bridgeman-scope-seven-lectures: Abstract, p.2: the notes state they form the basis for a seven lecture course on common tensor networks and algorithms. The authors' own statement of scope.
bridgeman-audience-limit: Abstract, p.2: the authors state the intended audience and that the relevance of many examples may be lost without a many-body physics or quantum information background. A caveat on their own notes.
bridgeman-material-from-memory: Acknowledgements, p.2: the authors say much of the material was reproduced from memory after the 2015 Gent summer school. A caveat on how the notes were produced.
bridgeman-tensor-network-definition: Section 1.3, p.9: the paper defines a tensor network. The sentence after the quotes gives the product-summed-over-internal-labellings value, so the whole value is in the passage.
bridgeman-stinespring-dilation: Section 2.4, pp.16-17: states the theorem for CPTP maps and derives it in Eqs 2.14 to 2.23 (isometry U from Kraus operators, then partial trace). The Kraus representation is a textbook tool used as a step, not a specific paper's theorem. The notes' own derivation is in the paper.
bridgeman-renyi-entropy-definition: Section 3, p.18: Eq. 3.3 defines the alpha-Renyi entropy. The S0 and von Neumann remarks follow directly from that definition (Tr rho^0 counts nonzero weights; alpha tending to 1).
bridgeman-mps-strong-area-law-exact: Section 3, pp.18-19: the exact successive-SVD construction (Eqs 3.4 to 3.7, 'general and exact') is in the paper. With at most c nonzero Schmidt weights per cut the bond dimension is at most c, giving the N d c^2 count. Condition quoted: S0 <= log c along every cut. The counting is simple, but the construction is exact.
bridgeman-mps-peps-not-scalable-preparat: Section 3.1, p.20: the authors caveat the PEPS view of MPS as a preparation procedure (post-selection, not generally scalable). A caveat on the construction they present. The word 'generically' is not proved here.
bridgeman-mps-gauge-freedom: Section 3.3.2, p.23: the paper defines gauge transformations as description changes that leave the state invariant, shows B_j = M A_j M^-1 gives the same state in Eqs 3.42 to 3.44, and notes M needs only a left inverse. 'Not all MPS represent different states' follows from this.
bridgeman-quantum-phase-definition: Section 4.1, p.28: 'for our purposes... we will say that two states are in the same phase if...'. The paper's own working definition.
bridgeman-lemma1-u-transfer-matrix-eigen: Lemma 1, Section 4.4, pp.30-31: stated for a unitary u and an injective MPS tensor, and proved in the paper by Cauchy-Schwarz (Eqs 4.12 to 4.18). The proof is written out, though 'translated into TNN from Ref. [8]'. It uses the unique full-rank fixed point rho of injectivity.
bridgeman-lemma2-equality-condition: Lemma 2, Section 4.4, pp.31-32: both directions proved in the paper. The only-if direction uses equality in Cauchy-Schwarz, invertibility of full-rank rho, and the injectivity assumption that the only norm-1 eigenvalue is the nondegenerate +1. Eq. 4.19 is a diagram garbled in the text layer, but the statement and proof are in the passage.
bridgeman-theorem1-symmetries-push-throu: Theorem 1, Section 4.4, pp.33-34: stated and proved in the paper (purity bound, Eqs 4.32 to 4.36, then Lemma 2). The standing assumption is an injective MPS tensor (Section 4.2), which the value does not repeat. 'Local symmetry' is used without a separate definition. The 'exponential decay' step is brief but argued.
bridgeman-dmrg-tebd-variational-setup: Section 5, p.37: the paper states the approach it presents (Rayleigh quotient minimisation over MPS of bounded bond dimension, Eq. 5.1) and that DMRG and TEBD differ in the variation step.
bridgeman-dmrg-key-heuristic: Sections 5.1, pp.37-38: the notes describe the DMRG algorithm they present as iterated single-tensor optimisations, after noting the objective is quadratic in each tensor. A description of the presented algorithm.
bridgeman-dmrg1-local-step-eigenvector: Section 5.1.1, pp.38-39: the DMRG1 local step as the paper presents it, reduced to Eq. 5.10 with the MPS in mixed canonical form, solved by the minimum eigenvector of Hermitian H_i, plus the sweeping. Algorithm description. The Rayleigh quotient fact used is textbook.
bridgeman-dmrg1-bond-dimension-limit: Section 5.1.1, p.39: the authors state the limitation of the one-site algorithm they present (fixed bond dimension, no gentle growth, no information on the chosen bond dimension). It follows from the one-site update as defined. Footnote 11 notes other methods exist, which the value does not contradict.

theory_low.bridgeman-ladder-bubbling-cost: Section 1.4, pp.9-10: a worked argument read from diagrams (Eqs 1.14 to 1.17), with no formal statement or proof. The first quote starts mid-sentence across a page break. An informal cost argument.
theory_low.bridgeman-2d-grid-contraction-exponentia: Section 1.4, p.10: a perimeter argument ('it is clear that') for single-tensor bubbling only. Not a proof, and 'generically exponential' is not shown.
theory_low.bridgeman-contraction-sharp-p-complete: Section 1.5, p.11: the e and n tensor construction is outlined. The NP-completeness of q-colouring is cited [8] and the #P-completeness is cited [9]. Relies on cited results, not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.bridgeman-bell-basis-pauli-vectorisation: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 2.1, p.14: the Bell states are written as vectorised Paulis, but the inner product correspondence is only asserted ('Thus we see'), with no conditions or proof.
theory_low.bridgeman-teleportation-deterministic: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 2.2, p.15: a diagrammatic calculation (Eqs 2.5 to 2.7) gives |psi>/2. The probability 1/4 and the determinism are read off it, not set out as a result with conditions. The first quote is the tail of a sentence.
theory_low.bridgeman-gate-teleportation-clifford: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 2.2.1, p.15: the Clifford correction being a Pauli is asserted with a footnote definition only. No derivation of the claim.
theory_low.bridgeman-aklt-hamiltonian-unique-gapped: Section 3.2, p.21: 'It is simple to check' with no check given. Uniqueness and gap are asserted, and the AKLT cite [9] is the source.
theory_low.bridgeman-cluster-state-scalable-mps-pre: Section 3.2, p.22: a short remark that the PEPS tensor is a unitary circuit (Eq. 3.33). No stated conditions or proof, and 'one of the exceptional cases' is the authors' claim.
theory_low.bridgeman-mps-exponential-decay-correlat: Section 3.3.1, pp.22-23: an informal transfer matrix argument. It assumes a unique dominant eigenvalue of E with the rest inside the unit disk ('we can normalise'), which is an assumption, not a proved fact for every MPS. No theorem statement or conditions. Concluding sentence cites [6].
theory_low.bridgeman-mps-renormalisation-transfer-m: Section 3.4, p.24: a one-line remark with no conditions or derivation. 'Never need to worry about discarding' is an interpretation.
theory_low.bridgeman-no-topological-order-1d-inject: Sections 4.3, pp.29-30: a sketch. E^k equals the fixed point only up to O(|lambda_2|^k) (Eq. 4.7), so the disentangling by the circuit V is approximate, and the claim 'constant number of sites' is not quantified. The result is credited to [3] ('we will see... [3]'). Not a proof in the paper.
theory_low.bridgeman-symmetry-virtual-action-phase-: Section 4.4, p.34: a one-sentence argument, 'any properties it has will be an invariant', with no stated theorem or conditions on which properties.
theory_low.bridgeman-injective-mps-symmetry-phases-: Aside 2, Section 4.4, p.35: the equivalence of projective phases is argued, but the identification with H2(G, U(1)) is cited [2, 10] and 'the only freedom is local rephasing' is asserted. Not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.bridgeman-imaginary-time-operator-bond-d: Section 5.2, p.40: asserted without proof. The quote stops before the qualifier 'for almost all tau', so the value drops a condition.
theory_low.bridgeman-suzuki-trotter-first-order: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 5.2, p.40: the first-order formula and its O(tau^2) error are stated, with no derivation. Families of higher order are cited [29].
theory_low.bridgeman-peps-entangled-plaquettes-no-m: Sections 6.1 and 6.2, pp.43-44: short constructive remarks (Eq. 6.6 for triplets; 'easy to see' for plaquettes). 'Small additional cost' is not quantified, and no conditions are stated.
theory_low.bridgeman-toric-code-ground-state-loops: Aside 3, pp.45-46: a construction argued in prose and diagrams ('not hard to convince yourself'). Not stated as a theorem with conditions, and no proof that all loop states are reached.
theory_low.bridgeman-2d-cluster-state-peps-bond-dim: Section 6.4, p.48: the tensor is given, but verification is left to Problem 6.3. The universality of the 2D cluster state for MBQC is cited [7, 8].
theory_low.bridgeman-peps-classical-partition-funct: Section 6.5.1, pp.50-51: a construction. 'Correlation functions are equal to classical ones' is asserted, with checking left to Problem 6.5. Credited to [3]. Not a stated and proved result.
theory_low.bridgeman-peps-algebraic-decay: Section 6.5.1, p.51: a reduction argument. That the classical model shows algebraic decay at criticality is background, and the PEPS correspondence rests on the unproved correlation claim above.
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-log-area-law-violation: Section 7.1, pp.53-54: an upper bound by bond counting. The O(log N) cut is read from a diagram ('straightforward to see') and attributed to [1, 2]. No theorem with conditions.
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-s-superoperator-unital-cp: Section 7.1, pp.54-55: a diagrammatic simplification (Eqs 7.4 to 7.9) with the Kraus reading of w, stated without a formal proof or conditions. Credited to [3].
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-algebraic-decay: Section 7.1, p.55: the argument is for operators at special sites in a ternary MERA, and the notes say it 'can be easily generalised' without showing it. The ~log N applications and Eq. 7.10 are not derived.
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-efficient-manipulation: Section 7.1, p.55: an argument that the isometric constraints keep operators local, credited to [10]. No theorem or cost bound is stated. 'Efficiently' is not quantified.
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-causal-cone-three-site: Section 7.1, p.55: read from a causal cone diagram (Eq. 7.11) with no formal statement or proof.
theory_low.bridgeman-mera-cluster-state-top-tensor: Section 7.4, p.57: the construction (Eq. 7.15 and top tensor |++>) is stated without derivation. Verification is left to the problems.
theory_low.bridgeman-appendix-particle-decay-ising: Appendix A.1, p.60: an explanatory reading of the transverse Ising MPO entries (Eqs A.1, A.2) for one example. No general theorem or proof.
